transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, honestly, what made me come in is I feel like... I don't know, like the warm part of me just shut off. 

I work as an order filler over at the distribution center, and usually when I clock out, I'm just so relieved. It's been a total mess there lately, they changed the whole barcode system and my scanner keeps freezing up on me, which completely messes up my pick rate. My manager is always breathing down our necks about it, so by the end of the shift my feet are killing me and I just want to go home. 

But anyway... usually when I get home from all that, I sit with my husband and we try to watch our shows. He's really into those cooking competitions right now, the ones where they have to use weird ingredients like squid ink or gummy bears or whatever. I normally love watching them, but lately... I just sit there. I know I should feel comfort, or even just a little happy to be off my feet and on the couch with him, but there’s just nothing there. It's like I can't feel it at all.
How long have you been feeling this way, where you don't feel comfort or happiness even during activities you used to enjoy?

It's been... um, about three weeks now. Yeah, three weeks. It all started right after this huge pallet collapsed at work and... it really injured my coworker. It was awful. 

But honestly, I'm not even surprised it happened because those wooden pallets we use are just ancient. They're supposed to inspect them, you know? But management just keeps reusing the busted ones with splintered wood and rusty nails sticking out everywhere because they don't want to pay for the heavy-duty plastic ones. My uncle worked at a warehouse over in Toledo and he said they switched to plastic years ago. He actually just retired, though. Bought a huge RV and is driving around the country with his wife and their two pugs. I think pugs are cute, but they always sound like they can't breathe, you know? I don't think I could sleep with a dog snoring like that in a tiny RV, especially with how bad my husband's allergies get in the spring. We tried to go camping once and he sneezed so much we just packed up and went to a diner instead.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, not just your usual shows with your husband?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it with other things. I guess I just haven't had the energy to do much else besides work and come home. It's just so exhausting at the warehouse, especially since they started making us park in the overflow lot. It's like a half-mile walk just to get to the employee entrance, and in this weather? It's miserable. The other day, it was pouring rain and I forgot my umbrella because I was rushing out the door. My husband usually reminds me, but he was on the phone with his sister. She just had a baby, a little girl. They named her Harper. It's a cute name, but it reminds me of that author, Harper Lee. We had to read *To Kill a Mockingbird* in high school, and I remember I had this teacher, Mr. Davis, who would always read the different parts in these really exaggerated voices. It was kind of funny, but also a little distracting. He retired a few years ago and moved to Florida, I think. A lot of people from my high school ended up moving away.
Have you found that you no longer enjoy other things that you used to, like spending time with friends, hobbies, or even simple things like a good meal or a favorite TV show?

Um... I mean, I guess it's hard to say about other things because I just really haven't been doing much of anything. Like I said, the shows are the main thing. We did try to get takeout from that Thai place we usually love on Friday, the one by the old movie theater? But I just kind of pushed the Pad Thai around my plate. It's usually my favorite, but I just wasn't feeling it. 

Speaking of that theater, they're tearing it down to build more luxury apartments. It's such a shame, because they used to do those midnight showings of old horror movies in October. My friend Sarah and I went to see *Night of the Living Dead* there a few years ago. Sarah actually just got a new job working at a bakery downtown. She brings home all these leftover pastries, which sounds great, but she says she's gaining so much weight from being around sugar all day. I told her she should just freeze them, but she says they don't taste the same when you thaw them out. I don't know, I freeze bread all the time and it seems fine to me. You just have to toast it right. But yeah... I don't know about the other stuff you asked about. I just haven't had the energy to try.
Have you found that you take little or no pleasure in most activities, or that nothing really interests you anymore?

I mean... I wouldn't say that absolutely nothing interests me. I just really haven't tried to do much lately to even know. But I still care about my plants on the porch, I guess. I have these cherry tomatoes that are finally starting to turn red. Well, the ones the squirrels don't get to first, anyway. 

My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she bought this giant plastic owl to scare them away from her garden, but I swear I saw a squirrel literally sitting on its head yesterday. It's ridiculous. She was so mad she came out yelling at them in her bathrobe. She has this really loud, bright floral robe, kind of like the ones from those old seventies catalogs? My grandmother used to wear those all the time. Hers was pink, though, and she always smelled like peppermint and... I don't know, mothballs or something. She used to keep those little strawberry candies wrapped in that foil in her purse, the ones that look like actual strawberries. I haven't seen those in a store in years. 

But, um... yeah, I don't know if I've lost interest in everything. I just haven't been doing much of anything to really tell you for sure.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past few weeks?

I wouldn't say depressed, really. Not all day. I'm mostly just stressed out and... and tired. Especially with the new forklift they brought in at the warehouse. It's supposed to be this new electric model that's better for the environment, but it makes this awful high-pitched whining noise the entire shift. It drives me absolutely crazy. 

My coworker, Dan, says he can't even hear it, but he listens to heavy metal on his earbuds the whole time anyway, even though we're not supposed to have them on the floor. He actually went to a Metallica concert last weekend and bought this vintage tour shirt that cost him like a hundred and fifty dollars. I just can't imagine spending that much on a t-shirt, you know? I usually just get my work shirts at Target when they go on clearance. They have those really soft v-necks, but they always shrink in the wash if you're not careful. I ruined three of them last month because our dryer's thermostat is broken. It just gets way too hot. My husband keeps saying he's going to watch a YouTube video and fix it, but he hasn't gotten around to it yet. So we just have wet clothes hanging all over the shower rod right now, which is a pain when you just want to take a quick shower after a long shift. 

But, um... what were you asking? Oh, feeling depressed. No, I don't think I feel like that all day. Just mostly worn out.
Have you felt down or sad most of the time, even if just a little, nearly every day for the past two weeks?

I mean, not really sad, no. I'm just... I guess I'm just so drained all the time. Speaking of being drained, my sister's dog just had puppies last week and she is completely exhausted. She has this golden retriever mix, Bailey, and she had a litter of six. They're super cute, but they are chewing on absolutely everything in her house. 

She actually had to hide all her good shoes on the top shelf of her closet. She has this one pair of leather boots she bought on a trip to Chicago—or maybe it was Boston? Anyway, she paid like three hundred dollars for them. I told her she was crazy spending that much on shoes when she mostly just works from home and goes to the grocery store anyway. I pretty much just wear my work sneakers everywhere. You really need good arch support when you're standing on those concrete floors at the warehouse all day, pulling orders. If you don't wear the right shoes, your feet are just screaming by the time you clock out. 

But, um... yeah, no, I don't think I've been feeling sad every day. Just really, really tired.
Have you felt a lack of energy or felt fatigued nearly every day for the past few weeks?

I mean, I know I just said I was drained, but I don't think it's like... zero energy every single day for weeks. Just regular tired from work, I guess. I actually tried to help it by getting one of those giant energy drinks from the vending machine in the breakroom yesterday. It was one of those neon green ones? It tasted exactly like melted gummy bears. 

My niece loves gummy bears, but she only eats the red ones. She’s four, and she throws an absolute fit if you try to give her a yellow or green one. My brother literally had to sit there and pick out all the red ones from a five-pound bag for her birthday party last weekend. They rented this huge princess bouncy castle for the backyard, which honestly looked like a lot of fun. I think you have to be under a certain weight limit to go in those, though, which is a shame, because jumping around in one of those seems like it would be a really good workout. I really should start working out again, maybe get a gym membership at that place down the street. They have an indoor pool, and I've always liked swimming. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, being fatigued. Yeah, no, I don't think it's anything unusual. Just normal tired from being on my feet.
Have you found that you have little interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy, not just your shows or meals, but in general?

Well, yeah, actually... that's kind of what made me come in. I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. Like, I'll sit with my husband on the couch after work, or try to watch my regular shows, and I know I should feel comfort, or at least a little happy, but there's just... nothing there. 

It's so weird, sitting on that couch and feeling nothing. We bought that couch at IKEA a few years ago. It's one of those sectionals where you can lift up the chaise part and store blankets inside. It's super practical, but putting it together was a nightmare. My husband and I spent like six hours on a Sunday trying to figure out the instructions because there aren't any words, just those little cartoon guys pointing at screws. We ended up with three extra wooden dowels and a weird metal bracket left over, which I'm pretty sure is not supposed to happen. We keep waiting for the whole thing to just collapse while we're watching TV, but it's held up pretty well so far. We did spill coffee on one of the cushions, though. I tried using that stain remover spray you see on TikTok, the one in the purple bottle? It didn't work at all, it just made the stain smell like fake lavender. 

But, um... yeah. I just don't feel anything good right now, even when I'm doing things I usually like. It's just blank.
Have you felt down or hopeless on most days, even if just a little, for the past two weeks?

I mean, no, not really hopeless. I don't feel like everything is doomed or anything. The only thing that feels hopeless lately is trying to get my husband to eat anything green. I actually tried to sneak some grated zucchini into a meatloaf on Tuesday. I saw it in this video on Facebook, from one of those cooking pages where they do everything in fast motion? The lady in the video had this amazing food processor that just shredded it in two seconds. I had to use a regular box cheese grater, and I ended up scraping my knuckles on it. 

It bled so much I had to put three bandaids on it, and then I couldn't even wash the dishes properly because I didn't want the bandaids to get soggy. Soggy bandaids are the absolute worst feeling. I usually try to buy those waterproof ones, the clear ones that stick really hard to your skin, but they always leave that weird sticky gray ring when you finally peel them off. You have to scrub it with rubbing alcohol just to get the residue off. We actually use rubbing alcohol at the warehouse sometimes to get the sticker adhesive off the metal racks when they change the inventory labels. The smell always reminds me of the nurse's office in middle school. Our school nurse had this huge jar of cotton balls sitting right next to a bowl of peppermints, which always seemed like a weird combination. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, feeling down or hopeless. No, I don't think so. It's not sadness or feeling hopeless, it's just... like I said, that blank feeling.
Have you felt down or low, even a little bit, most of the time during the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Well, I think you just asked me that, didn't you? About feeling down or hopeless? Like I said, it's not really a sad or low feeling. It's not like I'm crying all day or anything. I don't even remember the last time I cried, actually. Maybe when we watched that movie with the dog? The one where the dog waits for the owner at the train station for like, ten years. My husband refused to watch it with me because he said it was too depressing, so I watched it by myself on a Sunday afternoon while he was out washing the car. 

He's obsessed with keeping that car clean. It's a Honda Civic, nothing fancy, but he treats it like it's a Ferrari. He buys all these special waxes and microfiber towels from the auto parts store. He even has a tiny little vacuum that plugs into the cigarette lighter to get the crumbs out of the seats. I tried to use it once to clean up some spilled potting soil on the porch, but it barely had enough suction to pick up a single leaf. I ended up just sweeping it into the bushes with a broom. We have these big azalea bushes in the front yard, and they bloom these crazy bright pink flowers every spring. My neighbor hates them because the petals blow into her driveway, but she's always complaining about something. Last week she complained that the mailman was walking too heavily on her sidewalk. Like, how do you even measure that? 

But anyway... yeah, no. I don't feel down or low most of the day. It's really just that numb, blank thing I was telling you about.
Have you found that you have little interest or pleasure in almost all activities, not just the ones you've mentioned, for most of the day, more days than not over the past few weeks?

Well, I mean, I feel like you keep asking me the same thing over and over. It's just like I said before, honestly. That's exactly why I made the appointment to come in. I just feel like the warm part of me completely shut off. Like, I'll sit with my husband on the couch, or I'll try to watch my shows after my shift at the warehouse, and I know I'm supposed to feel comfort, or at least a little happy, but there's just... nothing. 

It's just totally blank. Even when I try to do other things I usually like, it's just the same. Like, I used to love going to the garden center on Saturdays. We have this huge nursery out by the highway, and they have these massive greenhouses that smell like wet dirt and fertilizer. It's the best smell. But the last time I went, I bought this little succulent, one of those ones that look like little green pebbles? I brought it home and put it on the windowsill above the kitchen sink, right next to this old ceramic rooster my aunt gave me when we moved in. The rooster is actually a sponge holder, but the sponges always get kind of gross and mildewy if you leave them in there too long. You have to run them through the dishwasher to get the smell out. We actually need a new dishwasher, ours makes this horrible grinding noise during the rinse cycle. My husband says it's just the water pump, but it sounds like a garbage disposal eating a spoon. We tried to call a repair guy, but they charge like a hundred dollars just to come look at it. You could practically buy a new one for that on Black Friday. 

But, um, yeah. It's not just my shows or meals. It's everything. I just don't feel any of those good feelings right now.
Have you felt down or had a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Okay, I feel like I'm taking a crazy test right now, because you literally just asked me that, didn't you? Like, almost word for word. It's still no. I'm not sad or low. It's just that blank feeling I keep trying to explain. 

But all these repeating questions, it really reminds me of those mandatory safety modules we have to do at the warehouse every six months. They make us sit in the breakroom and click through these computer slides about proper lifting techniques, and they ask the exact same question five different ways at the end just to make sure you didn't fall asleep. The guy in the training video always wears this neon green back brace that nobody actually uses in real life. My supervisor, Gary, tried to make everyone wear them last year because corporate was doing an audit, but they just make you sweat so much. It gets incredibly hot near the loading docks in the summer. We have these giant industrial fans, but all they do is blow the hot air around and kick up all the dust from the cardboard boxes. 

The dust gets right in your eyes, too. I had to start buying those special lubricating eye drops, the ones that come in the little individual plastic vials? Because my eye doctor said the regular bottles get contaminated if you accidentally touch the tip to your eyelashes. He has this really nice office, actually, with a huge saltwater fish tank right in the middle of the waiting room. It has one of those little blue tang fish, like from that cartoon movie with the talking fish. I could sit and watch that tank for hours, they just kind of glide around and don't have to worry about anything. 

But... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, the low mood thing. Yeah, no, still not feeling low or down. Just numb.

Anyway, she paid like three hundred dollars for them. I told her she was crazy spending that much on shoes when she mostly just works from home and goes to the grocery store anyway. I pretty much just wear my work sneakers everywhere. You really need good arch support when you're standing on those concrete floors at the warehouse all day, pulling orders. If you don't wear the right shoes, your feet are just screaming by the time you clock out. 

But, um... yeah, no, I don't think I've been feeling sad every day. Just really, really tired.

patient.answer:
I mean, I know I just said I was drained, but I don't think it's like... zero energy every single day for weeks. Just regular tired from work, I guess. I actually tried to help it by getting one of those giant energy drinks from the vending machine in the breakroom yesterday. It was one of those neon green ones? It tasted exactly like melted gummy bears. 

My niece loves gummy bears, but she only eats the red ones. She’s four, and she throws an absolute fit if you try to give her a yellow or green one. My brother literally had to sit there and pick out all the red ones from a five-pound bag for her birthday party last weekend. They rented this huge princess bouncy castle for the backyard, which honestly looked like a lot of fun. I think you have to be under a certain weight limit to go in those, though, which is a shame, because jumping around in one of those seems like it would be a really good workout. I really should start working out again, maybe get a gym membership at that place down the street. They have an indoor pool, and I've always liked swimming. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, being fatigued. Yeah, no, I don't think it's anything unusual. Just normal tired from being on my feet.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, actually... that's kind of what made me come in. I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. Like, I'll sit with my husband on the couch after work, or try to watch my regular shows, and I know I should feel comfort, or at least a little happy, but there's just... nothing there. 

It's so weird, sitting on that couch and feeling nothing. We bought that couch at IKEA a few years ago. It's one of those sectionals where you can lift up the chaise part and store blankets inside. It's super practical, but putting it together was a nightmare. My husband and I spent like six hours on a Sunday trying to figure out the instructions because there aren't any words, just those little cartoon guys pointing at screws. We ended up with three extra wooden dowels and a weird metal bracket left over, which I'm pretty sure is not supposed to happen. We keep waiting for the whole thing to just collapse while we're watching TV, but it's held up pretty well so far. We did spill coffee on one of the cushions, though. I tried using that stain remover spray you see on TikTok, the one in the purple bottle? It didn't work at all, it just made the stain smell like fake lavender. 

But, um... yeah. I just don't feel anything good right now, even when I'm doing things I usually like. It's just blank.

patient.answer:
I mean, no, not really hopeless. I don't feel like everything is doomed or anything. The only thing that feels hopeless lately is trying to get my husband to eat anything green. I actually tried to sneak some grated zucchini into a meatloaf on Tuesday. I saw it in this video on Facebook, from one of those cooking pages where they do everything in fast motion? The lady in the video had this amazing food processor that just shredded it in two seconds. I had to use a regular box cheese grater, and I ended up scraping my knuckles on it. 

It bled so much I had to put three bandaids on it, and then I couldn't even wash the dishes properly because I didn't want the bandaids to get soggy. Soggy bandaids are the absolute worst feeling. I usually try to buy those waterproof ones, the clear ones that stick really hard to your skin, but they always leave that weird sticky gray ring when you finally peel them off. You have to scrub it with rubbing alcohol just to get the residue off. We actually use rubbing alcohol at the warehouse sometimes to get the sticker adhesive off the metal racks when they change the inventory labels. The smell always reminds me of the nurse's office in middle school. Our school nurse had this huge jar of cotton balls sitting right next to a bowl of peppermints, which always seemed like a weird combination. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, feeling down or hopeless. No, I don't think so. It's not sadness or feeling hopeless, it's just... like I said, that blank feeling.

patient.answer:
Well, I think you just asked me that, didn't you? About feeling down or hopeless? Like I said, it's not really a sad or low feeling. It's not like I'm crying all day or anything. I don't even remember the last time I cried, actually. Maybe when we watched that movie with the dog? The one where the dog waits for the owner at the train station for like, ten years. My husband refused to watch it with me because he said it was too depressing, so I watched it by myself on a Sunday afternoon while he was out washing the car. 

He's obsessed with keeping that car clean. It's a Honda Civic, nothing fancy, but he treats it like it's a Ferrari. He buys all these special waxes and microfiber towels from the auto parts store. He even has a tiny little vacuum that plugs into the cigarette lighter to get the crumbs out of the seats. I tried to use it once to clean up some spilled potting soil on the porch, but it barely had enough suction to pick up a single leaf. I ended up just sweeping it into the bushes with a broom. We have these big azalea bushes in the front yard, and they bloom these crazy bright pink flowers every spring. My neighbor hates them because the petals blow into her driveway, but she's always complaining about something. Last week she complained that the mailman was walking too heavily on her sidewalk. Like, how do you even measure that? 

But anyway... yeah, no. I don't feel down or low most of the day. It's really just that numb, blank thing I was telling you about.

patient.answer:
Well, I mean, I feel like you keep asking me the same thing over and over. It's just like I said before, honestly. That's exactly why I made the appointment to come in. I just feel like the warm part of me completely shut off. Like, I'll sit with my husband on the couch, or I'll try to watch my shows after my shift at the warehouse, and I know I'm supposed to feel comfort, or at least a little happy, but there's just... nothing. 

It's just totally blank. Even when I try to do other things I usually like, it's just the same. Like, I used to love going to the garden center on Saturdays. We have this huge nursery out by the highway, and they have these massive greenhouses that smell like wet dirt and fertilizer. It's the best smell. But the last time I went, I bought this little succulent, one of those ones that look like little green pebbles? I brought it home and put it on the windowsill above the kitchen sink, right next to this old ceramic rooster my aunt gave me when we moved in. The rooster is actually a sponge holder, but the sponges always get kind of gross and mildewy if you leave them in there too long. You have to run them through the dishwasher to get the smell out. We actually need a new dishwasher, ours makes this horrible grinding noise during the rinse cycle. My husband says it's just the water pump, but it sounds like a garbage disposal eating a spoon. We tried to call a repair guy, but they charge like a hundred dollars just to come look at it. You could practically buy a new one for that on Black Friday. 

But, um, yeah. It's not just my shows or meals. It's everything. I just don't feel any of those good feelings right now.

Okay, I feel like I'm taking a crazy test right now, because you literally just asked me that, didn't you? Like, almost word for word. It's still no. I'm not sad or low. It's just that blank feeling I keep trying to explain. 

But all these repeating questions, it really reminds me of those mandatory safety modules we have to do at the warehouse every six months. They make us sit in the breakroom and click through these computer slides about proper lifting techniques, and they ask the exact same question five different ways at the end just to make sure you didn't fall asleep. The guy in the training video always wears this neon green back brace that nobody actually uses in real life. My supervisor, Gary, tried to make everyone wear them last year because corporate was doing an audit, but they just make you sweat so much. It gets incredibly hot near the loading docks in the summer. We have these giant industrial fans, but all they do is blow the hot air around and kick up all the dust from the cardboard boxes. 

The dust gets right in your eyes, too. I had to start buying those special lubricating eye drops, the ones that come in the little individual plastic vials? Because my eye doctor said the regular bottles get contaminated if you accidentally touch the tip to your eyelashes. He has this really nice office, actually, with a huge saltwater fish tank right in the middle of the waiting room. It has one of those little blue tang fish, like from that cartoon movie with the talking fish. I could sit and watch that tank for hours, they just kind of glide around and don't have to worry about anything. 

But... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, the low mood thing. Yeah, no, still not feeling low or down. Just numb.
